question: Which of the following is an example of public sector industry in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) under the Ministry of Heavy Industries, Government of India, engaged in power plant equipment manufacturing. (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र उद्योग — भारत हेवी इलेक्ट्रिकल्स लिमिटेड)

 

• It was incorporated in 1964 and is headquartered in New Delhi, with major manufacturing units at Bhopal, Haridwar, Tiruchirapalli, Hyderabad and other locations.

 

• A public sector industry (undertaking) is one in which majority ownership and management control rests with the government (Central or State).

 

• BHEL is one of India's largest engineering and manufacturing enterprises and a key player in the power, transmission, industry, transportation, renewable energy and defence sectors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Maharatna PSUs include Coal India Limited, NTPC, ONGC, SAIL, and Indian Oil Corporation.

 

NOTE

 

• Bajaj Auto (Option 2): A private sector company, part of the Bajaj Group, manufacturing two-wheelers and three-wheelers.

 

• Dabur (Option 3): A private sector Indian consumer goods company known for ayurvedic and natural products.

 

• Tata Iron Steel Company (Option 4): Now Tata Steel, a private sector company under the Tata Group, India's first integrated steel plant.

question: In which of the following years was Pro Kabaddi League established in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) was established/launched in 2014 as a professional kabaddi league in India, modelled on the format of the Indian Premier League. (प्रो कबड्डी लीग — 2014 में स्थापित)

 

• Its inaugural season was held from 26 July to 31 August 2014, broadcast on Star Sports, with 8 franchise teams.

 

• Jaipur Pink Panthers won the first season of the Pro Kabaddi League.

 

• The league is organised by Mashal Sports in partnership with Star Sports and is credited with popularising kabaddi as a professional sport in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PKL currently features teams such as Patna Pirates, U Mumba, Bengal Warriors, and Puneri Paltan, among others.

 

• Patna Pirates hold the record for most PKL titles.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (2015, 2016, 2013): These years are incorrect; the league's establishment and first season both took place in 2014, though subsequent seasons were held in later years.

question: The Vedangas are Hindu auxiliary disciplines that originated in ancient times and are linked to the study of the Vedas. These are _________ in number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is six.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vedangas are six auxiliary disciplines developed to aid the correct understanding, recitation and application of the Vedas. (वेदांग — छह अंग)

 

• The six Vedangas are: Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (rituals), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chandas (metre), and Jyotisha (astronomy).

 

• They are considered essential for the study, correct pronunciation and ritual application of Vedic texts and are traditionally regarded as limbs (angas) of the Veda-Purusha.

 

• Each Vedanga developed into its own specialised field of Sanskrit scholarship over time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Upanga (auxiliary limbs), distinct from Vedangas, include Puranas, Nyaya, Mimamsa and Dharmashastra.

 

• Panini's Ashtadhyayi is a key text of the Vyakarana Vedanga.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (five, seven, four): These numbers are incorrect; the Vedangas are traditionally enumerated as exactly six disciplines.

question: What was the actual growth rate of the first five-year plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.6%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56), based on the Harrod-Domar model, targeted a growth rate of 2.1% but achieved an actual growth rate of 3.6%. (प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना — वास्तविक वृद्धि दर 3.6%)

 

• The plan focused primarily on agriculture, irrigation and power projects, including river valley projects like the Bhakra Nangal and Hirakud dams.

 

• It was formulated under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, who headed the Planning Commission.

 

• The success of the First Plan, exceeding its target, was largely attributed to good harvests in the final years of the plan period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission was established in 1950, and the First Five-Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956.

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) focused on rapid industrialisation, based on the Mahalanobis model.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (4.2%): Not the actual growth rate of the First Plan.

 

• Option 2 (2.6%): Not the actual growth rate of the First Plan.

 

• Option 4 (2.1%): This was the targeted, not the actual, growth rate of the First Plan.

question: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?
option_1: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
option_2: Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
option_3: Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
option_4: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The five Fs of indirect (faecal-oral) transmission describe the main routes by which pathogens from faeces reach a new host: Flies, Fingers, Fomites, Food and Fluid. (पांच एफ — मल-मौखिक संचरण के मार्ग)

 

• This framework, part of the classic F-diagram used in public health and sanitation, explains how disease-causing organisms travel from faeces to the mouth via these five indirect pathways.

 

• Flies mechanically carry pathogens from faeces to food; fingers get contaminated through poor hand hygiene; fomites are contaminated inanimate objects/surfaces; food and fluid (water) become vehicles of infection when contaminated.

 

• Diseases such as cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea commonly spread through these indirect faecal-oral routes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Breaking these transmission pathways through safe sanitation, handwashing, safe drinking water and food hygiene is central to preventing faecal-oral diseases.

 

• The extended F-diagram in sanitation literature also includes Faeces and Fields as sources/pathways.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid): Not part of the recognised five Fs; 'fruit' and 'flu' are not among the standard terms.

 

• Option 3 (Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit): Incorrect; 'friends' and 'fruit' are not part of the standard five Fs.

 

• Option 4 (Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit): Incorrect; the fifth term is 'fluid', not 'fruit'.

question:
Match the points under Column A with those under Column B.

Column A

i. Annelida

ii. Arthropoda

iii. Echinodermata

iv. Platyhelminthes

Column B

a. Tapeworm

b. Sea star

c. Ant

d. Earthworm
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annelida is correctly matched with Earthworm (d); annelids are segmented worms, and the earthworm is a classic example. (वलयकृमि — एनेलिडा, केंचुआ)

 

• Arthropoda is correctly matched with Ant (c); arthropods have jointed legs and a chitinous exoskeleton, and ants belong to this phylum.

 

• Echinodermata is correctly matched with Sea star (b); echinoderms are marine animals with spiny skin and radial symmetry, and the sea star (starfish) is a typical example.

 

• Platyhelminthes is correctly matched with Tapeworm (a); platyhelminthes are flatworms, and the tapeworm is a well-known parasitic example.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Annelida also includes leeches and marine polychaetes; Arthropoda is the largest animal phylum, including insects, crustaceans and arachnids.

 

• Echinodermata includes sea urchins and sea cucumbers, while Platyhelminthes includes flukes in addition to tapeworms.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4: Each of these pairs at least one phylum with the wrong example organism, breaking the correct one-to-one correspondence given in Option 1.

question: The Election Laws Amendment Bill passed in the Parliament recently seeks to implement certain electoral reforms. One of them is the eligibility date. Till now, only one date – 1 January was considered for deciding eligibility with respect to age. What reform does the Bill seek in this regard?
option_1: Introducing two dates – 1 January and 1 June
option_2: Eliminating the idea of eligibility date – enrolment throughout the year
option_3: Introducing four dates – 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October
option_4: Introducing three dates – 1 January, 1 May, 1 September
solution_text:
The correct answer is Introducing four dates – 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 amended the Representation of the People Act, 1950, to replace the single qualifying date (1 January) with four qualifying dates in a calendar year: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. (चुनाव कानून संशोधन विधेयक — चार अर्हता तिथियां)

 

• This reform allows a person turning 18 after 1 January to register as a voter without waiting for a full year, enabling four opportunities annually to enrol in the electoral roll instead of one.

 

• The Act was passed by both Houses of Parliament in December 2021, and also enabled linking of Aadhaar with voter ID on a voluntary basis and made electoral rolls gender-neutral for service voters.

 

• It aims to reduce the exclusion of eligible young voters who would otherwise have to wait almost a year to be added to the rolls.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Act also substituted the term 'wife' with 'spouse' in the Representation of the People Act, 1950, making it gender-neutral for service personnel.

 

• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Two dates – 1 January and 1 June): Incorrect; the Act specifies four dates, not two.

 

• Option 2 (Eliminating eligibility date – enrolment throughout the year): Incorrect; a fixed set of qualifying dates was retained, just increased from one to four.

 

• Option 4 (Three dates – 1 January, 1 May, 1 September): Incorrect; the actual dates introduced are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.

question: In July 2020, which state initiated the 'Ashirwad Scheme' to extend financial support for a daughter's marriage who belongs to a family earning a lower income?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ashirwad Scheme was initiated by the Government of Punjab in July 2020 to provide financial assistance for the marriage of daughters belonging to low-income SC/ST/BC and minority families. (आशीर्वाद योजना — पंजाब सरकार)

 

• The scheme provides a fixed cash grant (revised periodically) to help meet marriage expenses, aimed at reducing the financial burden on economically weaker families.

 

• Eligible beneficiaries must be residents of Punjab, with family income below a prescribed limit, and the benefit can be availed for up to two daughters per family.

 

• The scheme is implemented online through the dedicated Ashirwad portal under the Department of Social Justice, Empowerment and Minorities, Punjab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Punjab also runs the Shagun Scheme, a related welfare scheme with similar objectives that was later merged/renamed under Ashirwad.

 

• Other states run comparable schemes, e.g., Rajasthan's Mukhyamantri Kanyadan Yojana and Uttar Pradesh's Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah Yojana.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Runs the Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah/Vivah Anudan Yojana, not the Ashirwad Scheme.

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Runs schemes like Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah Yojana, not the Ashirwad Scheme.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Runs the Mukhyamantri Kanyadan Yojana, not the Ashirwad Scheme.

question: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 207 of the Constitution, a Money Bill cannot be introduced in a State Legislature except on the recommendation of the Governor. (धन विधेयक — राज्यपाल की पूर्वानुमति)

 

• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly (the lower/only directly elected house), not in the Legislative Council where one exists.

 

• This mirrors the provision at the Union level under Article 117, where a Money Bill requires the President's prior recommendation.

 

• Once passed by the Assembly, a Money Bill goes to the Legislative Council (in bicameral states), which can only recommend changes within 14 days; the Assembly may accept or reject these recommendations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 199 of the Constitution defines what constitutes a Money Bill at the state level.

 

• The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill, and this certification is final.

 

NOTE

 

• Auditor General (Option 2): No such constitutional office exists by this name in India; it is not relevant to Money Bill introduction.

 

• Finance Minister (Option 3): Introduces the Money Bill in the House but does not give the constitutional recommendation required — that is the Governor's role.

 

• CAG (Option 4): The Comptroller and Auditor General audits government accounts; it has no role in recommending Money Bills.

question: According to Census of India 2011, what is the gap between male and female literacy rate in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.68%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the male literacy rate was 82.14% and the female literacy rate was 65.46%, giving a gender gap of 16.68 percentage points. (जनगणना 2011 — साक्षरता अंतर 16.68%)

 

• The overall literacy rate of India as per Census 2011 was 74.04%.

 

• Among states, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate, while Bihar recorded the lowest.

 

• The literacy gender gap has been narrowing over successive censuses, reflecting improved female education access, though a gap persists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

• The 2021 Census was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (21.59%, 18.30%, 24.84%): These figures do not match the actual male-female literacy gap recorded in Census 2011, which is 16.68 percentage points.

question: In which year was the Digital India mission launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Digital India mission was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 1 July 2015 with the aim of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. (डिजिटल इंडिया — 1 जुलाई 2015)

 

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and rests on three key vision areas: digital infrastructure, digital governance and services, and digital literacy.

 

• Key initiatives under Digital India include DigiLocker, MyGov, BHIM, Common Services Centres (CSCs), and UMANG.

 

• The programme aims to bridge the digital divide and improve e-governance and online public service delivery across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP), launched in 2006, was an earlier precursor initiative to Digital India.

 

• BharatNet is a key infrastructure project under Digital India aimed at providing broadband connectivity to Gram Panchayats.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (2014, 2016, 2017): These years are incorrect; Digital India was formally launched in 2015.

question: Who among the following players is related to table tennis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manika Batra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manika Batra is a leading Indian table tennis player, known for winning multiple medals at the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games, and for reaching a career-best world ranking inside the top 25. (मनिका बत्रा — टेबल टेनिस खिलाड़ी)

 

• She created history at the 2018 Commonwealth Games (Gold Coast) by winning individual gold, along with team gold, women's doubles bronze and mixed doubles bronze.

 

• She has represented India at multiple Olympic Games, including Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (now Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna) for her contributions to table tennis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian table tennis players include Sharath Kamal and Sathiyan Gnanasekaran.

 

NOTE

 

• Manish Narwal (Option 1): A Paralympic shooter, gold medallist at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.

 

• K Srikanth (Option 3): A leading Indian badminton player, former World No. 1.

 

• Pankaj Advani (Option 4): A multiple-time world champion in billiards and snooker.

question: Which of the following gases emits red light when electricity is passed through it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neon gas emits a characteristic reddish-orange glow when an electric current is passed through it at low pressure, which is why it is widely used in neon signs/advertising lights. (नियॉन गैस — लाल प्रकाश उत्सर्जन)

 

• Neon is a noble (inert) gas, present in trace amounts in the Earth's atmosphere, and belongs to Group 18 of the periodic table.

 

• Different noble/inert gases emit different characteristic colours when electrically excited: e.g., helium glows pale peach/pink-orange, argon glows violet/lavender, and krypton glows greenish-white.

 

• The colour results from the specific wavelengths of light emitted as excited electrons in the gas atoms return to lower energy states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neon was discovered in 1898 by Sir William Ramsay and Morris Travers.

 

• Neon lighting was pioneered commercially by French engineer Georges Claude in the early 20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen (Option 2): Emits a pinkish-violet glow in a discharge tube, not red.

 

• Argon (Option 3): Emits a violet/lavender-blue glow, not red.

 

• Helium (Option 4): Emits a pale peachy/pinkish-orange glow, not the characteristic red of neon.

question: Chand Bardai’s famous literary work ________, mentions Prithviraj Chauhan‘s love story and heroic deeds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prithviraj Raso.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chand Bardai, the court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan, composed the epic poem Prithviraj Raso, a major work of early Hindi (Brajbhasha) literature. (पृथ्वीराज रासो — चंद बरदाई)

 

• The text narrates the life, love story (with Sanyogita) and heroic deeds/battles of Prithviraj Chauhan, the last Hindu king of Delhi before the Ghurid conquest.

 

• It is considered one of the earliest and most important works of medieval Hindi (Rajasthani/Brajbhasha) literature, though historians debate how much of it is historically reliable versus embellished poetic narrative.

 

• Chand Bardai is regarded as one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Prithviraj Chauhan's court.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan famously fought the First (1191) and Second (1192) Battles of Tarain against Muhammad of Ghor.

 

• Later folk retellings and oral traditions kept the Prithviraj Raso narrative alive across North Indian culture.

 

NOTE

 

• Harakeli Nataka (Option 1): A Sanskrit drama attributed to the Kakatiya king Prataparudra, unrelated to Prithviraj Chauhan.

 

• Abhidhana Chintamani (Option 2): A Sanskrit lexicon (dictionary) composed by the Jain scholar Hemachandra.

 

• Rajamartanda (Option 4): A commentary on the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, written by King Bhoja of Malwa.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters is known as ‘Deshbandhu’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chittaranjan Das, popularly known as 'Deshbandhu' (friend of the nation), was a prominent Bengali freedom fighter, lawyer and founder of the Swaraj Party in 1923 along with Motilal Nehru. (देशबंधु — चित्तरंजन दास)

 

• He was famous for the Alipore Bomb Case (1908), where he successfully defended Sri Aurobindo.

 

• He served as the President of the Indian National Congress at the Gaya Session (1922).

 

• The Swaraj Party, which he co-founded, advocated contesting elections to legislative councils and obstructing British governance from within.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Motilal Nehru, co-founder of the Swaraj Party, was given the title 'Pandit'.

 

• Chittaranjan Das's residence in Kolkata was later donated for public use and is associated with several nationalist activities.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 1): Known as the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi; founder of the Servants of India Society.

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 2): A revolutionary freedom fighter, associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association; not called 'Deshbandhu'.

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose (Option 3): Known as 'Netaji', founder of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj).

question: Buddhadev Dasgupta is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Buddhadev Dasgupta was an eminent Indian classical musician renowned as a sarod player, belonging to the Shahjahanpur-Senia gharana. (बुद्धदेव दासगुप्ता — सरोद वादक)

 

• He was a disciple of Ustad Radhika Mohan Maitra and was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

• The sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument known for its deep, resonant tone, widely used in North Indian (Hindustani) classical music.

 

• He was also known for his efforts in preserving and reviving classical instrumental traditions and training numerous students.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous sarod players include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan.

 

• The sarod is believed to have evolved from the Afghan rebab.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarangi (Option 2): A bowed string instrument; noted exponents include Ustad Sultan Khan and Ram Narayan.

 

• Bansuri (Option 3): A bamboo flute; noted exponents include Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

• Mridangam (Option 4): A South Indian percussion instrument used in Carnatic music; noted exponents include Palghat Mani Iyer.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizens?
option_1: To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
option_2: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
option_3: To cherish and follow the noble ideas that inspired our national struggle for freedom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandatory national service of 5 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties, listed under Article 51A of the Constitution (added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee), do not include any provision for mandatory national service. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, including duties like respecting the Constitution, upholding sovereignty, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and developing scientific temper.

 

• 'To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform' and 'to safeguard public property and to abjure violence' are both genuine, existing Fundamental Duties.

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced directly by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 11th Fundamental Duty (to provide opportunities for education to children aged 6-14) was added later by the 86th Constitutional Amendment, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Scientific temper, humanism, inquiry and reform): This is genuinely listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(h).

 

• Option 2 (Safeguard public property, abjure violence): This is genuinely listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(i).

 

• Option 3 (Cherish and follow noble ideals of the freedom struggle): This is genuinely listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(b).

question: What is the product formed when zinc and sulphuric acid react?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zinc sulphate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid, it produces zinc sulphate (ZnSO₄) and releases hydrogen gas (H₂): Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑. (जिंक सल्फेट — जिंक और सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल की अभिक्रिया)

 

• This is a classic example of a displacement reaction, where a more reactive metal (zinc) displaces hydrogen from the acid.

 

• The evolved hydrogen gas can be tested by bringing a burning matchstick near the mouth of the test tube, which produces a characteristic 'pop' sound.

 

• Zinc reacts similarly with other dilute acids (like hydrochloric acid) to form the corresponding zinc salt and hydrogen gas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zinc sulphate is used in agriculture as a micronutrient fertiliser and in medicine as a dietary zinc supplement.

 

• Metals like copper, being less reactive than hydrogen, do not react with dilute sulphuric acid to release hydrogen.

 

NOTE

 

• Zinc hydroxide (Option 2): Would form from a reaction of zinc salts with a base (alkali), not from the direct reaction of zinc metal with sulphuric acid.

 

• Zinc sulphide (Option 3): Formed from the reaction of zinc with sulphur, not with sulphuric acid.

 

• Zinc oxide (Option 4): Formed by the reaction of zinc with oxygen (burning in air), not with sulphuric acid.

question: Hindustani singer Pandit Venkatesh Kumar was honoured with 'Kalidas Samman-2022' by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kalidas Samman is a prestigious award instituted in 1980 by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, given for outstanding contributions in classical music, dance, theatre, and plastic arts. (कालिदास सम्मान — मध्य प्रदेश सरकार)

 

• Hindustani classical vocalist Pandit (M.) Venkatesh Kumar was honoured with the Kalidas Samman 2022 in the classical music category.

 

• The award is named after the legendary Sanskrit poet and dramatist Kalidasa, and is presented by the Madhya Pradesh government's Directorate of Culture.

 

• It carries a cash prize along with a citation and is considered one of India's most prestigious cultural honours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kalidas Samman is awarded across categories such as classical music, classical dance, theatre, and plastic arts (visual arts).

 

• Madhya Pradesh also organises the Kalidas Samaroh, an annual classical arts festival held in Ujjain.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these state governments confer the Kalidas Samman; it is exclusively awarded by the Madhya Pradesh government.

question: In which form of exchange are goods used as medium of exchange?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barter exchange.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a barter exchange (barter system), goods and services are directly exchanged for other goods and services without the use of money as a medium of exchange. (वस्तु विनिमय — बार्टर प्रणाली)

 

• This system was prevalent before the invention of money and required a 'double coincidence of wants' — both parties needed to want what the other was offering.

 

• Barter exchange has limitations such as lack of a common measure of value, indivisibility of goods, and difficulty in storing value, which led to the evolution of money as a medium of exchange.

 

• Despite its limitations, barter is still practised informally in some rural or localised economies today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The evolution of exchange systems generally moved from barter → commodity money → metallic money → paper currency → credit/digital money.

 

• Modern economies primarily use fiat currency, whose value is backed by government decree rather than a physical commodity.

 

NOTE

 

• Online exchange (Option 1): Refers to digital/electronic transactions using money, not goods, as the medium.

 

• Credit exchange (Option 2): Involves deferred payment arrangements, not goods used directly as a medium of exchange.

 

• Currency exchange (Option 3): Refers to exchanging one currency for another, not goods being used as a medium of exchange.

question: Gangaur Festival, Pushkar Fair, Nagaur Fair and Urs Fair are the popular fairs and festivals of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gangaur Festival, Pushkar Fair, Nagaur Fair and Urs Fair (Ajmer) are all well-known and popular fairs/festivals celebrated in the state of Rajasthan. (गणगौर, पुष्कर मेला — राजस्थान)

 

• Gangaur is a festival dedicated to Goddess Gauri (Parvati), celebrated widely across Rajasthan by married and unmarried women.

 

• The Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Mela) is a famous camel and livestock fair held annually in Pushkar, near Ajmer.

 

• The Urs Fair is held at the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in Ajmer, commemorating his death anniversary, while the Nagaur Fair is another major cattle fair of the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Rajasthan fairs/festivals include the Desert Festival (Jaisalmer), Teej, and the Kumbhalgarh Festival.

 

• Rajasthan is renowned for its vibrant folk culture, forts, palaces and desert tourism.

 

NOTE

 

• Tripura, Punjab and Maharashtra (Options 2, 3, 4): These states have their own distinct fairs and festivals, but not the Gangaur, Pushkar, Nagaur and Urs fairs mentioned, which are specific to Rajasthan.

question: ______ leaves are used to make bidis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tendu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tendu leaves (from the tree Diospyros melanoxylon) are used to wrap bidis (Indian hand-rolled cigarettes). (तेंदू पत्ता — बीड़ी निर्माण)

 

• Tendu leaf collection is an important minor/non-timber forest produce (NTFP) activity, providing seasonal livelihood to millions of tribal and forest-dwelling people, especially in states like Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Maharashtra.

 

• Tendu is also known as the 'Indian ebony' or East Indian ebony tree; besides bidi wrapping, its fruit is edible.

 

• The trade of tendu leaves is regulated by state governments through cooperative societies in several states to ensure fair prices to collectors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh is one of the largest producers of tendu leaves in India.

 

• Tendu leaves are collected mainly during the summer season (April-June).

 

NOTE

 

• Neem (Option 1): Its leaves are used for medicinal and pesticidal purposes, not for wrapping bidis.

 

• Champa (Option 2): A flowering plant, not used for making bidis.

 

• Betel (Option 3): Betel leaves are chewed (as paan) with areca nut, not used to make bidis.

question: Which of the following hills is located in the Eastern Ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shevaroy hills.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Shevaroy Hills are located in the Eastern Ghats, in the Salem district of Tamil Nadu, and are known for their coffee and orange plantations, with Yercaud as the main hill station. (शेवरॉय पहाड़ियां — पूर्वी घाट)

 

• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of hills running along India's eastern coast, from Odisha through Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and include ranges like the Shevaroys, Javadi and Palkonda hills.

 

• The Shevaroy Hills form part of the larger complex of hill ranges within the Eastern Ghats system in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Unlike the continuous Western Ghats, the Eastern Ghats are broken up by several rivers flowing from the Deccan plateau to the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Eastern Ghats ranges include the Javadi Hills, Palkonda Range, and Nallamala Hills.

 

• The Anamudi peak, the highest in South India, lies in the Western Ghats.

 

NOTE

 

• Naga hills (Option 1): Located in the northeastern hill ranges (Nagaland/Manipur), not in the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Khasi hills (Option 2): Located in the northeastern hill ranges of Meghalaya, not in the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Anamudi hills (Option 4): Located in the Western Ghats, Kerala, and includes the highest peak in South India.

question: Who established Shantiniketan and when?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravindranath Tagore, 1901.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore established Shantiniketan in 1901, in West Bengal, initially as an experimental school named 'Brahmacharya Ashram', later evolving into Visva-Bharati University. (शांतिनिकेतन — रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर, 1901)

 

• Shantiniketan was founded on the principles of learning close to nature, with an emphasis on creativity, art, and holistic education, away from rigid conventional classroom teaching.

 

• Tagore's father, Debendranath Tagore, had earlier acquired the land at Shantiniketan (originally called Bhubandanga) and set up an ashram there before Rabindranath established the school.

 

• Visva-Bharati University, established in 1921 by expanding this institution, was declared a Central University and Institution of National Importance in 1951, and Rabindranath Tagore served as its chancellor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shantiniketan was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his work Gitanjali, becoming the first non-European to receive it.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi, 1910 (Option 1): Gandhi was not the founder of Shantiniketan, though he visited it and shared a close relationship with Tagore.

 

• Ravindranath Tagore, 1905 (Option 3): Incorrect year; Tagore established Shantiniketan in 1901, not 1905.

 

• Devendranath Tagore, 1915 (Option 4): Devendranath Tagore (Rabindranath's father) had earlier set up an ashram at the site, but the school/institution of Shantiniketan was founded by Rabindranath Tagore in 1901, not by Devendranath in 1915.

question: Which of the following institutes was founded by Mrinalini Sarabhai who was a Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer?
option_1: Sri Thyagaraja College of Music and Dance
solution_text:
The correct answer is Darpana Academy of Performing Arts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai, a renowned Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer, founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in 1949 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, along with her husband, scientist Vikram Sarabhai. (दर्पण अकादमी — मृणालिनी साराभाई)

 

• The academy promotes classical Indian dance, drama, music and puppetry, and has trained generations of performing artists, including her daughter, dancer Mallika Sarabhai.

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was honoured with the Padma Bhushan for her contributions to Indian classical dance.

 

• She trained in Bharatanatyam and Kathakali and was closely associated with reviving and popularising classical dance traditions across India and internationally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vikram Sarabhai, her husband, is known as the father of the Indian space programme and founder of ISRO.

 

• Mallika Sarabhai, their daughter, is also a well-known classical dancer and activist, and currently directs the Darpana Academy.

 

NOTE

 

• Sri Thyagaraja College of Music and Dance (Option 1): Not founded by Mrinalini Sarabhai.

 

• Nrityanjali Institute of Performing Arts (Option 2): Not founded by Mrinalini Sarabhai.

 

• Nalanda Nritya Kala Mahavidyalaya (Option 4): Founded by Kumudini Lakhia, a noted Kathak dancer, not by Mrinalini Sarabhai.
